novel_features.name: Find photographic subjects near a place
novel_features.description: Finds things worth photographing near a place — water towers, lighthouses, brutalist buildings, piers, viewpoints — by name rather than by OpenStreetMap tag.
novel_features.rationale: Overpass takes a query language, not a subject. This maps photographic vocabulary onto the correct tag combinations, builds valid Overpass QL, and retries across mirrors when one is overloaded.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this whenever someone wants to know what is worth shooting around a place, without needing to know OpenStreetMap tagging.

novel_features.name: Browse the subject taxonomy
novel_features.description: Lists every subject type the CLI knows how to find, with the OpenStreetMap tags behind each one.
novel_features.rationale: The curated mapping from photographic vocabulary to OSM tags is the actual product; showing it makes the tool inspectable rather than magic.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to see what can be searched before running near, or to check what tags a subject type actually resolves to.

novel_features.name: Subjects along a drive
novel_features.description: Finds subjects inside a corridor between two places, so a drive can be planned around what is worth stopping for.
novel_features.rationale: Requires building a bounding corridor from two geocoded points and querying inside it. Overpass has no notion of a route; every wrapper leaves this to the caller.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when planning a drive or day trip and the question is what to stop for on the way.

novel_features.name: Export to GeoJSON
novel_features.description: Writes results as GeoJSON for opening in a map, a Leaflet page, or any GIS tool.
novel_features.rationale: Overpass returns its own element format with centers split across fields; converting it to standard GeoJSON is left to every caller.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when the result needs to end up on a map rather than in a terminal.

novel_features.name: Mirror health
novel_features.description: Shows which Overpass mirrors are currently answering and how many rate-limit slots each has free.
novel_features.rationale: Public Overpass instances fall over under load independently; on 2026-07-26 three of four mirrors refused the same query while one served it. Knowing which is healthy is the difference between a working query and a mystery failure.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when queries are failing or slow, before assuming the query itself is wrong.

narrative.headline: Find things worth photographing by name instead of by OpenStreetMap tag, with automatic failover across Overpass mirrors.
narrative.value_prop: Overpass is a query language wearing a REST costume, and its public mirrors fall over independently under load. This maps photographic vocabulary — water towers, lighthouses, brutalist buildings, piers, observatories — onto the right tag combinations, builds valid Overpass QL, retries across mirrors, caches results locally, and exports GeoJSON.
narrative.auth_narrative: No credential at all. Both Overpass and Nominatim are keyless; they only require a descriptive User-Agent, which this CLI sends. Nominatim permits about one request per second and Overpass allocates a small number of concurrent slots per mirror, so the CLI paces itself and fails over rather than hammering one host.

quickstart.comment: See what subjects can be found before searching for one.
The core query: subjects by name near a place.
Check which Overpass instances are healthy if a query is slow.
Put the results on a map.

troubleshoots.fix: That mirror is overloaded, not your query. The CLI already retries across mirrors; run `overpass-pp-cli mirrors` to see which are healthy, or raise --timeout.

troubleshoots.symptom: No results for a subject you know exists
troubleshoots.fix: OpenStreetMap coverage is uneven and volunteer-contributed. Run `overpass-pp-cli types` to see the exact tags being queried, and widen --radius.

troubleshoots.symptom: Geocoding a place name returns the wrong country
troubleshoots.fix: Nominatim orders by relevance worldwide. Add a region to the query ("San Pedro, CA") or pass --country us.
Overpass allocates a couple of concurrent slots per mirror and large radii are expensive. Narrow --radius, or let the local cache serve a repeat query.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this when the task is finding physical things in the world worth going to look at — structures, viewpoints, industrial or architectural subjects — near a place or along a route. It also exposes raw Overpass QL for queries the curated taxonomy does not cover.

recipes.title: What is worth shooting near here
recipes.explanation: Maps the subject name to OSM tags, builds the query, and retries across mirrors.

recipes.title: See the tags behind a subject
recipes.explanation: Shows exactly which OpenStreetMap tags each subject type resolves to, so the search is inspectable.

recipes.title: Plan a drive around subjects
recipes.explanation: Builds a corridor between the two points and finds subjects inside it.

recipes.title: Narrow a verbose result payload
recipes.explanation: Overpass elements carry every OSM tag; --select with dotted paths returns only the fields needed.

recipes.title: Export for a map
recipes.explanation: Converts Overpass elements, whose coordinates live in different fields for nodes and ways, into standard GeoJSON.
